senses.gloss: f. (אֲרִי, אֲרָא) pointing at, argument, topic, subject.
units: <cite ref="Keritot 3b:29">Kerith. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>גבי כריתות דאי׳ וכ׳</he> in speaking of K’rithoth, where this (the punishment of extinction) is the subject proper, I may say, the general term of Sabbath &c. is introduced (relying on those places in the Mishnah where the respective laws are treated in detail).
<cite ref="Yoma 74a:9">Yoma 74ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אי משום הא לא א׳</he> were it only for this, there would be no argument (no difficulty).

<cite ref="Keritot 18a:41">Kerith. 18ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מאי א׳ כי וכ׳</he> why is the argument brought up only on the presumption (that he has eaten? Supposed, he had not eaten, would not the same argument hold good?).
<cite ref="Shabbat 101a:5">Sabb. 101ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מידי א׳</he> is this an argument (i.e. how can you compare two cases so unlike each other)?
